info.title: Tasker API
info.description: REST API of Tasker. The same API is served by the Tasker server (Server mode, JWT sign-in) and by the local daemon (Local mode, no sign-in, loopback only; every request is addressed to one workspace through the /w/{workspace} prefix). x-tasker-modes on an operation lists where it exists: server, local, daemon (control interface of the daemon, which has its own address and secret). Data is read through GraphQL (operation executeGraphQL, schema graphql/schema.graphql); this REST API changes data (POST, PATCH, DELETE), signs in, reports health and controls the daemon. PATCH changes only the fields that are sent (null or absent keep the value) and needs the version the client saw; DELETE takes it in the version query parameter. Errors are {error}; a conflict (409) also carries code: in_use (the entity is used), modified (someone changed it first: reload and retry), locked (someone is editing it, heldBy says who) or unsupported_format.

servers.description: Tasker server (Server mode): sign in with POST /api/auth/login and send the access token as a Bearer token
Tasker daemon (Local mode): no sign-in, loopback only; the workspace is the key of an open folder

200.description: A query result (application/json) or a subscription stream (text/event-stream)

post.summary: GraphQL endpoint: all reads and live changes
post.description: Reads go through GraphQL, not GET (schema: graphql/schema.graphql). Body: {query, operationName, variables}. A query returns application/json {data, errors}; an error answers 400, or 401 when sign-in is needed (Server mode). A subscription (workspaceChanges, the replacement of the old GET /events) answers text/event-stream: each result is one `data: <GraphQLResponse as JSON>` line followed by an empty line, lines starting with a colon are comments to ignore (`: connected` right after the connection opens, `: ping` every 20 seconds while idle). Treat a change as a hint to reload what it names; after a reconnect reload everything, events are not replayed.
